Both sexual and asexual means are used to increase the number of plants; seeds and multiplication of corms are the most common means of production, but [tissue culture](/wiki/Plant_tissue_culture "Plant tissue culture") can be used,[[114]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTERana2021-116) most commonly for saffron crocus. New corms are formed on top of the older corm which withers away, and cormels are produced from axillary buds.[[112]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDe_Hertogh_et_al201281-114) The production of new plants begins with harvested corms in late June to early July, after being graded by corm size the corms are stored around 22 °C (72 °F) until early October when they are moved to 17 °C (63 °F) until planted later in October and November; flowering occurs in March and the flowers are not removed. Crocuses are also forced to produce flowering plants out of season and the most common species used are *C. vernus* and *C. flavus*, and most of the corms used for forcing come from the Netherlands.[[115]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDe_Hertogh1992-117)

Spring flowering types are planted in fall, while fall-blooming types in late summer; typically, the corms are placed 3 to 4 inches (7.6 to 10.2 cm) deep in well-draining soil in areas with full sun exposure. They do not thrive in heavy clay soils or those that are damp, especially during their summer dormancy period.[[116]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTETenenbaum2003-118) Commercial crops are produced on raised beds and slopes, to ensure adequate drainage, while horticulturalists often plant on sand beds for the same purpose.[[117]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTERuksans201120-119) Spring flowering types also do well in areas with deciduous trees, where they flower and produce leaves before the trees completely leaf-out. In Brazil, most important cities are on the coast or close to it. State capitals are also, commonly, the largest city of their states. Notable exceptions to this are [Vitória](/wiki/Vit%C3%B3ria,_Brazil "Vitória, Brazil"), the capital of [Espírito Santo](/wiki/Esp%C3%ADrito_Santo "Espírito Santo"), and [Florianópolis](/wiki/Florian%C3%B3polis "Florianópolis"), the capital of [Santa Catarina](/wiki/Santa_Catarina_(state) "Santa Catarina (state)").

There are also non-capital metropolitan areas, for example, in [São Paulo state](/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo_(state) "São Paulo (state)") ([Campinas](/wiki/Campinas "Campinas"), [Santos](/wiki/Santos_(S%C3%A3o_Paulo) "Santos (São Paulo)"), [Paraíba Valley](/wiki/Para%C3%ADba_Valley "Paraíba Valley"), [Sorocaba](/wiki/Sorocaba "Sorocaba"), [Ribeirão Preto](/wiki/Ribeir%C3%A3o_Preto "Ribeirão Preto") and [Franca](/wiki/Franca "Franca")), [Minas Gerais](/wiki/Minas_Gerais "Minas Gerais") ([Steel Valley](/wiki/Vale_do_A%C3%A7o "Vale do Aço")), [Rio Grande do Sul](/wiki/Rio_Grande_do_Sul "Rio Grande do Sul") ([Sinos Valley](/wiki/Porto_Alegre "Porto Alegre")), and Santa Catarina ([Itajaí Valley](/wiki/Vale_do_Itaja%C3%AD "Vale do Itajaí")), amongst others.

[São Paulo](/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo "São Paulo") and [Rio de Janeiro](/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro "Rio de Janeiro") are far larger than any other Brazilian cities. São Paulo's influence in most economic aspects can be noted in a national (and even international) scale; Rio de Janeiro – partially due to its former status as the national capital – still host various large [corporations' headquarters](/wiki/List_of_Brazilian_companies "List of Brazilian companies"), besides being Brazil's cultural center with respect to [film production](/wiki/Cinema_of_Brazil "Cinema of Brazil") and other such televised media. [Brasília](/wiki/Bras%C3%ADlia "Brasília"), the capital of Brazil, is its 3rd biggest city.

About $2 billion of investment income is annually distributed to fund operations.[[103]](#cite_note-104)
Harvard's ability to fund its degree and financial aid programs depends on the performance of its endowment; a poor performance in fiscal year 2016 forced a 4.4% cut in the number of graduate students funded by the [Faculty of Arts and Sciences](/wiki/Harvard_Faculty_of_Arts_and_Sciences "Harvard Faculty of Arts and Sciences").[[104]](#cite_note-105)
Endowment income is critical, as only 22% of revenue is from students' tuition, fees, room, and board.[[105]](#cite_note-106)

Italian was the official language in Monaco until 1860, when it was replaced by French.[[37]](#cite_note-miglioverde-40) This was due to the annexation of the surrounding [County of Nice](/wiki/County_of_Nice "County of Nice") to France following the [Treaty of Turin (1860)](/wiki/Treaty_of_Turin_(1860) "Treaty of Turin (1860)").[[37]](#cite_note-miglioverde-40)

The [Grimaldi](/wiki/Grimaldi_Family "Grimaldi Family"), [princes of Monaco](/wiki/Princes_of_Monaco "Princes of Monaco"), are of Ligurian origin; thus, the traditional national language is [Monégasque](/wiki/Mon%C3%A9gasque_language "Monégasque language"), a variety of [Ligurian](/wiki/Ligurian_(Romance_language) "Ligurian (Romance language)"), now spoken by only a minority of residents and as a common second language by many native residents. The first issue of *The New York Times*—initially called the *New-York Daily Times*—was published on Thursday, September 18, 1851. The name was changed in 1857 to *The New-York Times* after the evening edition was suspended, and the hyphen was dropped in 1896.[[7]](#cite_note-NYTimes_20260104-9)

Mamet is the daughter of American playwright, essayist, screenwriter, and film director [David Mamet](/wiki/David_Mamet "David Mamet") and actress [Lindsay Crouse](/wiki/Lindsay_Crouse "Lindsay Crouse"). Her father is the grandson of Polish Jews[[6]](#cite_note-tt-6) and she says her given name is Polish and Russian.[[7]](#cite_note-7) Her maternal grandfather was playwright [Russel Crouse](/wiki/Russel_Crouse "Russel Crouse") and her maternal great-grandfather was educator [John Erskine](/wiki/John_Erskine_(educator) "John Erskine (educator)"). She has a sister, Willa, who is a singer, and two half-siblings: [Clara](/wiki/Clara_Mamet "Clara Mamet"), also an actress and director; and Noah. She lived in New England until age five when her mother moved to [Pacific Palisades, California](/wiki/Pacific_Palisades,_California "Pacific Palisades, California"), with Willa and Zosia.[[8]](#cite_note-nyt1-8) After finishing high school, Mamet decided to pursue acting instead of going to college.[[9]](#cite_note-9)

In 2012, Mamet was cast by [Judd Apatow](/wiki/Judd_Apatow "Judd Apatow") in the [HBO](/wiki/HBO "HBO") series *[Girls](/wiki/Girls_(TV_series) "Girls (TV series)")*. She has subsequently appeared as a regular in television series such as *[The Flight Attendant](/wiki/The_Flight_Attendant "The Flight Attendant")*, *[The Decameron](/wiki/The_Decameron_(TV_series) "The Decameron (TV series)")*, and *[Laid](/wiki/Laid_(American_TV_series) "Laid (American TV series)")*.

Sales for Bryant's replica jersey fell significantly.[[413]](#cite_note-422) In September 2004, the assault case was dropped by prosecutors after the accuser decided not to testify at the trial. Afterward, Bryant agreed to apologize to her for the incident, including his public *[mea culpa](/wiki/Mea_culpa "Mea culpa")*: "Although I truly believe this encounter between us was consensual, I recognize now that she did not and does not view this incident the same way I did. It was Curie's hope that naming the element after her native land would publicize its lack of independence. This element was the first one discovered by the Curies while they were investigating the cause of [pitchblende](/wiki/Uraninite "Uraninite") [radioactivity](/wiki/Radioactivity "Radioactivity"). Pitchblende, after removal of the radioactive elements [uranium](/wiki/Uranium "Uranium") and [thorium](/wiki/Thorium "Thorium"), was more radioactive than the uranium and thorium combined. This spurred the Curies to search for additional radioactive elements. They first separated out polonium from pitchblende in July 1898, and five months later, also isolated [radium](/wiki/Radium "Radium").[[18]](#cite_note-nbb-18)[[38]](#cite_note-c1-38)[[43]](#cite_note-c2-43) German scientist [Willy Marckwald](/wiki/Willy_Marckwald "Willy Marckwald") successfully isolated 3 milligrams of polonium in 1902, though at the time he believed it was a new element, which he dubbed "radio-tellurium", and it was not until 1905 that it was demonstrated to be the same as polonium.[[44]](#cite_note-44)[[45]](#cite_note-45)
